explain.say: Mould spores are everywhere in the air, far too small to see. When one lands on something damp with food in it, like bread or fruit, it sprouts.

explain.say: Thin threads called hyphae grow through the bread, digesting it as they go. Most of the mould is hidden inside, so even a small spot means threads have spread through the food.

faq.q: Is it safe to cut the mould off bread?
faq.a: No. Mould threads spread through soft foods like bread, so throw the whole thing away. Hard cheese is different: food safety agencies say you can cut away at least 2.5 centimetres around and below the spot.
asks: Can I eat bread with a bit of mould?

faq.a: By spores. Each patch releases millions of light spores into the air, which land on other food and start new patches. Sniffing or shaking mouldy food can puff spores out too.
asks: Why does mould spread to other food?

faq.a: The colour comes from the spores. Different moulds make different coloured spores, like black bread mould or the green and blue of Penicillium.

faq.q: What makes food go mouldy faster?
faq.a: Warmth, damp and air. Bread in a warm, humid kitchen goes mouldy quickly, while drying, freezing or keeping food cool slows mould down.
asks: How do I stop bread going mouldy?

faq.a: No. Some moulds make blue cheese and Brie, soy sauce and the antibiotic penicillin. But mould growing on food by accident can make toxins, so it is best not to eat it.

facts: Black bread mould is a fungus called Rhizopus stolonifer.
Food safety guidance says to cut at least 2.5 cm around and below a mould spot on hard cheese, but to throw away soft foods with mould.
Mould spores are present in almost all indoor and outdoor air.

quiz.say: Why is it unsafe just to scrape the mould off soft bread?

options.show: Scraping makes the mould grow back
options.say: Scraping makes the mould grow back

quiz.why: The visible fuzz is only the spore stalks; the feeding threads run through the whole soft loaf.

wrong.1: The danger is the hidden threads and possible toxins, not the colour.
wrong.2: The real problem is mould already inside, not regrowth from scraping.
